prompt: Should cops have qualified immunity?

The qualified immunity doctrine prevents plaintiffs from suing officers in their individual capacities unless it can be shown that the officer violated a clearly established statutory or constitutional right of the plaintiff. This protects officers from wrongful lawsuits, allowing them to focus on their job without fear of being sued for performing their duties. At the same time, it does not prevent plaintiffs from bringing lawsuits when there is evidence of actual misconduct by an officer or when an officer exceeds the scope of his or her authority.
